verdict.rationale: Authenticator documents its own Cloud Backup that lets you restore saved accounts on a new device after signing in, so the core migration path exists. It does not move all tokens: backup covers OTP codes only for 'eligible' personal and third-party accounts, and passkeys are device-bound and never leave the original phone. Setup also requires a personal Microsoft account (and iCloud on iOS), which a user confirms. Missing for 10: transfer of all credential types including passkeys and work accounts, evidence of a single guided transfer step, hands-on corroboration of the restore flow.

support.subject: As an everyday user, moving to a new phone transfers all my tokens in one guided step

citations.quote: if you lose your mobile or get a new device, you can sign in to restore previously saved accounts
Turn on the Cloud Backup toggle. Select a Microsoft personal account where the backup will be stored.
Microsoft Authenticator backs up one-time password codes for eligible Microsoft personal accounts and third-party accounts, such as LinkedIn and Facebook.
Passkeys in the Authenticator app are device-bound to ensure that they never leave the device they were created on.
